subject: VPN/Peering egress — concurrency & latency acceptance plan
messages:
From: Sophie Chan <sophie.chan@finmetrics.com>

Cc: Luis Ortega <luis.ortega@finmetrics.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo — network/egress constraints + top-level targets

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. I wanted to capture the perf targets and a couple of constraints from our side so we can align on an acceptance plan. High level: we are evaluating a private deployment (VPC + customer-managed VPN/peering) for latency-sensitive scoring of financial models.

FinMetrics targets and constraints (initial):
- Latency: p95 inference (end-to-end client -> model -> client) target ~50ms; p99 target ~120ms. Streaming sessions (server-sent tokens) should keep initial token <= 80ms most of the time.
- Throughput/concurrency: expected sustained concurrency 600-800 concurrent scoring sessions during market hours; occasional spikes to 1,200 concurrent sessions for short bursts up to 2–3 minutes.
- Egress: traffic must exit via our VPN to a single peered gateway; we can provision up to 3 Gbps on the tunnel for tests, but typical live capacity is 1.5 Gbps.
- Networking: conservative MTU (1500), vendor managed Cisco ISR on our side; BGP or static routing ok but we prefer BGP for failover.

We captured an initial traceroute and a small pcap during the demo—attached as network-path-traceroute.txt.

Next steps we need from Redwood to scope acceptance testing:
1) A concise test plan for private deployment validation (latency, p95/p99, concurrency ramp, streaming jitter).
2) Any requirements for TLS termination location, NAT, or IP ranges that need to be whitelisted.
3) A proposed test window (we are available next Tue/Wed mornings).

Happy to loop in our security team if you need an SOC or compliance contact.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Chan
Director, Platform Engineering — FinMetrics

Subject: Re: Post-demo — network/egress constraints + top-level targets

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear summary and the traceroute. Pulling together a short acceptance plan and a test harness we can run from both sides. Summary / clarifications from our side below.

High-level alignment (Redwood):
- We can target p95 <= 60ms and p99 <= 120ms for typical scoring flows during the acceptance window; streaming initial token target 80ms p95 (matches yours). Final SLA language will depend on the exact sequence length and model variant we pin for tests.
- Concurrency: we can validate up to 1,200 concurrent sessions in our dedicated test harness; we'll run sustained 800-session runs for 30–60 minutes plus spike tests (1,200 for 3 minutes).
- Egress throughput: we'll exercise up to 3 Gbps during the tests. For production we recommend reserving at least 2x expected peak (so 3 Gbps is a good starting point given your peaks).

Technical asks from Redwood to FinMetrics (so our test engineers can pre-configure):
- Confirm whether you want TLS terminated at the peering gateway (you mentioned VPN); if TLS is terminated within your network then we will do mutual TLS to the peered endpoint.
- Provide the customer-managed VPN IP ranges and ASN if using BGP.
- If possible, enable a test host behind the same gateway to run our synthetic traffic generator (we will provide commands).

Acceptance test plan (we will handoff a YAML test plan — attached as redwood-private-test-plan.yaml):
- Baseline: single-session latencies across 1000 samples (cold and warm cache).
- Ramp: linear ramp to 800 concurrent sessions over 10 minutes, sustain 30 minutes, measure p50/p95/p99 latencies and token emit jitter for streaming.
- Spike: 1,200 concurrent sessions for 3 minutes to validate graceful degradation and circuit-breaker behavior.
- Network stress: 1 minute 3 Gbps egress test to validate tunnel throughput and MTU stability.

Internal notes: Diego will own the test harness and packet captures; Jonas will run the on-site connectivity preflight with your network team; Marissa will coordinate dates and DocuSign if procurement needs formalization.

Proposed test window: Tue Jul 13 or Wed Jul 14 between 08:00–11:00 PT. If those don't work, propose alternatives.

Attached: redwood-private-test-plan.yaml (test config + command list).

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

@all — quick technical clarifications so we don't waste the test window. Forwarding Sophie's traceroute inline for context.

On Mon, Jul 5, 2027 at 09:12 Sophie Chan <sophie.chan@finmetrics.com> wrote:
> (traceroute attached)

Questions / suggestions from our infra side:
- Routing: BGP is preferred for automated failover. If you cannot enable BGP, static routes are fine but we'll need a scheduled re-route test to validate our fallback.
- MTU & fragmentation: keep MTU at 1500 during initial testing; if you have jumbo frames enabled on internal nets, please flag it. Fragmentation increases CPU on some appliances and can spike tail latencies.
- Keepalive/jitter: for streaming sessions we recommend an application-level heartbeat (every 10s) and will tolerate up to 30ms jitter before we mark streams as degraded.
- VPN throughput: please validate that your Cisco ISR tunnel can sustain 3 Gbps; if not, we can split across two tunnels but will need BGP and route preferences.
- IP ranges: please share 2x subnets (service and test) and a contact for your network engineer.

I'll attach a quick script we use to run iperf-like checks and warm TCP connections: vpn-test-commands.sh. If you can provision a host we can run the first round unilaterally and share captures.

Diego
